about: The expert council, item 8, part 1 (queue expert-council): environment design. Architects and behavioural scientists agree that people mostly do what their surroundings make easy. So do not rely on willpower: change the room, the phone and the defaults once, and the right thing happens by itself. This file is the household layer (places and defaults); the estate's own catalogue of set-and-forget reversals lives in governance/environment.py and is not repeated here. Paraphrased from common practice; content only, the screen is not built yet. Not medical advice.

loop.cue: One change a week, offered on the weekend when there is time to move things (calendar item proposed: council-environment-reset, weekly, 10 minutes).
loop.smallestStep: Move one thing: put the wanted thing in sight, or the unwanted thing out of reach.
loop.reward: Each change is done once and stays done; the list of changes made is the progress.
loop.environment: This system is itself the environment step of every other loop.
loop.review: Monthly: which change stuck without effort? Keep those. Which one did you work around? Redesign it, do not try harder.
loop.constraint: Other people in the home. Agree shared spaces together; change your own corner first.

laws.text: What you see, you do. Put the cue for a wanted habit where your eyes land.
Every extra step halves the chance. Add steps to what you want less; remove them from what you want more.
The option that happens when you do nothing wins. Make the right one the default.
A place used for one thing triggers that thing. Keep the bed for sleep and the desk for work.
Tomorrow's first step should need no decision: laid out, charged, packed.

changes.do: Charge the phone outside the bedroom; use a simple alarm clock.
Set screens to night mode on a schedule and use a warm, low lamp in the last hour.
A filled bottle on the desk and the bedside every morning.
Fruit on the counter at eye level; sweets and fried snacks in an opaque box on a high shelf, or not bought.
Walking shoes and clothes by the door before bed.
First phone screen: tools only (calendar, notes, maps, this app). Social and news apps off the first screen, signed out, badges off.
Allow notifications from people and the calendar only; everything else is read when you choose.
Clear the desk to today's one task before you leave it; close every tab not needed for it.
The current book on the pillow or by the kettle; the remote in a drawer.
A standing instruction on salary day moves savings out before you see them.
changes.undo: Cancel the instruction in the bank app.

changes.do: Remove saved cards from shopping sites and turn off one-click buying.
Unsubscribe from sale e-mails and messages for one month and see what you miss.
One tray by the door: keys, wallet, badge, medicines, the bag packed.
A basket for phones at meals, adults first.
Daily medicines next to the toothbrush, in a weekly box.
changes.careful: Keep medicines out of children's reach.

match.say: The app offers the change for the area the person marked weakest, or the habit they keep missing; never the whole list.

persona.who: A person who scrolls late and sleeps badly
An older person who forgets medicines
